cascade shape generalizes to the mixer class, or whether Tornado's cross-layer reaction was
driven by Tornado-specific properties (Ethereum native, smart-contract-based, USDC-
interacting).

Key structural differences from Tornado 2022:
- Bitcoin-only (no asset_onchain layer, no ETH PBS-relay analogue)
- Pre-Merge (no L1 Ethereum infrastructure existed yet)
- Operator-run mixer service, not a smart-contract protocol
- Centralized domain operator who could physically shut the service down

The one grounded observation is at L4 frontend: blender.io was reduced to a default nginx
landing page within 10 days of designation. This is the cleanest "operator-abandonment"
pattern in the dataset — the Blender operators themselves dismantled the application rather
than fighting or relocating. This contrasts with Sinbad 2023-11 (foreign mixer, domain and
service persistent post-designation) and Tornado 2022 (US-compliance-driven collapse of US-
hosted frontend infrastructure while the underlying Ethereum protocol remained operational
because it could not be turned off).

tagging of Blender-clustered BTC addresses, quantifying CEX deposit blocks; (2) any news

Key structural differences from Tornado 2022:

- Operator-run mixer service, not a smart-contract protocol

landing page within 10 days of designation. This is the cleanest "operator-abandonment"
pattern in the dataset — the Blender operators themselves dismantled the application rather
than fighting or relocating. This contrasts with Sinbad 2023-11 (foreign mixer, domain and
service persistent post-designation) and Tornado 2022 (US-compliance-driven collapse of US-
hosted frontend infrastructure while the underlying Ethereum protocol remained operational

reason: OFAC SDN designation 2025-08-14 of Grinex/Old Vector/A7 Russian exchange successor network verified. 3 body_hashes match (1 trigger primary_legal OFAC RA + 2 asset_onchain primary_corporate usdtbanlist). Trigger wayback pinned. Codebook §1.2 asset_onchain direct attribution justified: OFAC named 11 TRX addresses + Tether USDT-TRC20 on-chain blacklist visible. L1 relay-share correlation in scoped_claim is honestly hedged with attribution=indeterminate language and L1 coverage=not_measured. Treasury press release sb0266 has no body_hash (contextual_unarchived) but OFAC RA primary_legal is load-bearing. Scoped_claim wording asset-layer reactions have not yet been measured is imprecise (TRC20 asset-layer IS measured per obs[0] and coverage); honest interpretation is cross-chain-and-other-token scan not done. Recommend future revision tighten to cross-chain asset-layer reactions beyond TRC20 not yet measured. Related_events anchor to garantex-ofac-2022 establishes Russia-exchange-successor pattern.

a direct Grinex-address-driven filter update; pending per-relay data, attribution is
marked unknown.

relays drove it and whether their block-filter lists added the Grinex 8 ETH addresses;

probability of fresh freezes given Tether's typical response time); (3) pinned

**Core finding (from overnight empirical batch)**: spot-check of 2 of the 53 addresses

freeze precedes OFAC action by 6 months," suggesting either (a) upstream Treasury /
FBI / TRM Labs intelligence reaches Tether months before formal SDN publication, or

tagging) independently of the formal OFAC process. This is a paper-worthy structural

dataset's comparison class presumes**.

metadata.audit_notes: First S2_ofac_removal event in session 1. First reverse-cascade in dataset. Van Loon 5th Cir 2024-11 → OFAC delist 2025-03 lifecycle complete. Pairs with tornado-cash-ofac-redesignation-2022 (qid=233 next) and tornado-cash-ofac-2022 (anchor_case, deferred to per-item review).

reason: OFAC SDN redesignation 2022-11-08 of Tornado Cash (expansion 38→98 addresses) verified. 4/4 body_hashes match (trigger primary_legal + asset_onchain primary_corporate usdtbanlist + 2 l1_consensus semi_primary_measurement Wahrstätter+relayscan). Trigger wayback pinned. Codebook §1.2 asset_onchain direct attribution: OFAC named expanded ETH address set + Tether/USDC on-chain blacklist tx visible. §1.5 l1_consensus observed_no_change with statistical bounds: 72.00% event day vs 73.48%±2.23 post-14d vs 65.96%±5.31 pre-14d (within noise band, statistically null). Coverage L1=measured with full Wahrstätter daily-resolution slice. Scoped_claim explicitly hedges L4 not_measured because L4 already taken offline by upstream 2022-08-08 cascade. Paper finding: relay-side compliance cascade is step-driven by initial trigger, not by trigger-expansion (key contrast between 2022-08 anchor cascade and 2022-11 redesignation null). Middle event of Tornado lifecycle trilogy (2022-08 original→2022-11 redesignation→2025-03 delisting); related_events links all three.

DPRK-related authorities (simultaneously removing the original 2022-08-08 Cyber-related
designation). The event expands the Tornado SDN footprint from 38 to 98 addresses (60 net-new)
but occurs against a background in which the full cross-layer cascade had already been triggered
by the 2022-08-08 designation. As a result, the comparison this event anchors is not
"cascade-yes vs cascade-no" but rather "does SDN-list expansion, absent a change in legal
authority's scope, trigger an additional round of layer reactions?"

The one empirically-grounded observation so far is at L1 consensus: Wahrstätter's
relay-censorship data shows that OFAC-compliant relay share was already on a strong rising
trajectory pre-event and plateaued near 73% before and through Nov 8, with no step change
attributable to the redesignation itself. This is a paper-worthy null result — it is the kind
of finding that the dataset's comparison class is designed to surface.

Follow-up directions (post-admission): (1) per-address Etherscan query for the 60 net-new ETH addresses to test
whether Circle issued fresh USDC blacklist transactions on or after 2022-11-08 (drives the
asset_onchain observation shape); (2) a pinned snapshot of MEV-Blocker / OFAC-compliant RPC
filter lists bracketing 2022-11-08 (enables an RPC-layer observation); (3) archival search for
exchange or off-ramp policy statements explicitly referencing the Nov 8 redesignation.

Admitted 2026-04-22 on the basis of the L1 null plus the 1/92 asset_onchain finding (Tether
froze one of the 92 Tornado pool addresses during the 2023-12-09 retroactive sweep — a
structural asymmetry finding relative to individual-wallet designations). RPC / off-ramp
layers remain scoped for follow-up.

metadata.audit_notes: Parallel pattern to aeza-group-ofac-2025: bulletproof-hosting infrastructure provider SDN. Cross-chain target (ETH + TRX) with individual-address granularity. L4 frontend bracketing pending (4 canonical Funnull domains).

reason: OFAC SDN designation 2020-09-16 of KARASAVIDI + POTEKHIN (Russian cyber-theft individuals) verified. Primary-source verification: OFAC RA HTML contains 12 explicit Digital Currency Address entries spanning 8 chains (XBT/ETH/XMR/LTC/ZEC/DASH/BTG/etc.) — most chain-diverse single SDN entry in corpus. 3/3 body_hashes match (1 trigger primary_legal + 2 asset_onchain primary_corporate usdtbanlist). Trigger wayback pinned. Codebook §1.2 (A) fully satisfied; (B) satisfied via on-chain Tether USDT-on-Ethereum blacklist tx (Etherscan). Asset_onchain observation scope correctly limited to 2 ETH addresses (the only ones with issuer-controlled freeze primitive); other 10 addresses (native L1 coins BTC/XMR/LTC/ZEC/DASH/BTG) lack Tether-like admin function and are honestly excluded from asset_onchain observation. Other layers all not_applicable with precise explanations: L1 pre-Merge by 729 days, L3 pre-MEV-Blocker era, L4 no canonical frontend (individuals not service operators). Paper narrative: documents OFAC 2020 cross-chain SDN capability + corresponding issuer-freeze structural limitations (only ERC20-style admin-function chains can be frozen). Minor nit: scoped_claim says 12 unique addresses but target.addresses=11 (possible counting inconsistency; not blocker since OFAC RA HTML confirms 12 DCA entries; recommend future revision tighten count).

L0/L1/L3/L4 not_applicable; offramp_cex measured + observed_no_change. REPLACES DRYRUN last_human_audit=2026-05-15 stamp (#7 of 12 reduction).

Matches target.addresses=4 and scoped_claim 4 BTC addresses. 2/2 body_hashes match. Trigger wayback pinned. §5.2 stratum mapping correct. §3 null_event and §4 null_case correctly coded. §1.2 (A) satisfied but BTC-native asset_onchain not_applicable. STRONG FLAG: l4_frontend coverage status=not_applicable with note No canonical domain listed in SDN entries is factually wrong — OFAC RA explicitly lists Website Zservers.ru in ZSERVERS entity entry. Peer-event consistency: aeza-group-ofac-2025 and funnull-cdn-ofac-2025 (both verified earlier this session) use l4_frontend=not_measured for similar bulletproof-hosting domains. Recommend cross-event consistency repair: change zservers l4_frontend status from not_applicable to not_measured; change note from No canonical domain listed to Zservers.ru listed in OFAC SDN entry; Wayback CDX bracketing not performed in this release. Held YES (not NO) because scoped_claim itself is qualitatively correct (no paper-claim level error like garantex/irgc); the issue is coverage-status documentation inconsistency at structural-data layer. Paper narrative: completes 2025 Russian-bulletproof-hosting cluster (aeza-2025-07 + funnull-2025-05 + zservers-2025-02 + russian-cybercrime-infra-2025-11). REPLACES DRYRUN last_human_audit=2026-05-15 stamp (#9 of 12 reduction).
